literal: Shengzong merged the two prefectures to establish it.
idiomatic: Shengzong combined the two prefectures into this seat.

literal: Subordinate to Yanchang Palace; military affairs belonged to the Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.
idiomatic: Under Yanchang Palace; military affairs to the Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.

literal: Originally Bohai Yuexi County land, with Wan'an County merged to establish it.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Yuexi County merged with Wan'an County.

literal: Shuang Prefecture, Bao'an Army, lower, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Shuang Prefecture (Bao'an Army, lower), military commissioner.

literal: Bohai established Anding Commandery, long abolished.
idiomatic: Bohai once founded Anding Commandery, long since abolished.

literal: Ouli Monk King followed Taizong on the southern campaign and with captives from Zhen and Ding two prefectures built a city and established the prefecture.
idiomatic: Ouli Monk King followed Taizong south and with Zhen and Ding captives walled a city and founded the prefecture.

literal: Chagie was executed for regicide and it was confiscated.
idiomatic: Chagie's execution for regicide brought confiscation.

literal: Formerly subordinate to Yanchang Palace; later to Chongde Palace; military affairs to the Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.
idiomatic: First under Yanchang Palace; later Chongde Palace; military affairs to Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.

literal: Yin Prefecture, Fuguo Army, lower, cishi.
Originally Bohai Fu Prefecture; Taizu renamed it for silver smelting.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Fu Prefecture; Taizu renamed it for silver works.

literal: Subordinate to Hongyi Palace; military affairs belonged to the Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.
idiomatic: Under Hongyi Palace; military affairs to Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.

literal: Originally Bohai Fushou County; within the border was the old Yanjin fort, hence the rename.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Fushou County; an old Yanjin fort within the border gave the new name.

literal: Originally old Yuexi state land; Bohai established silver smelting and once established Yin Prefecture.
idiomatic: Originally Yuexi territory; Bohai ran silver smelting and once titled Yin Prefecture.

literal: Originally Bohai Youfu County land; Taizu established it with captives.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Youfu County; Taizu settled captives here.
An old Yongping Stockade had stood there.

literal: Tong Prefecture, Zhen'an Army, lower, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Tong Prefecture (Zhen'an Army, lower), military commissioner.

literal: Originally Han Xiangping County land; Bohai made it Dongping Stockade.
idiomatic: Originally Han Xiangping County; Bohai made Dongping Stockade.

literal: Taizu established the prefecture, army called Zhendong, later renamed.
idiomatic: Taizu founded the prefecture as Zhendong Army, later Zhen'an.

literal: Subordinate to Zhangmin Palace; military affairs belonged to the Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.
idiomatic: Under Zhangmin Palace; military affairs to Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.

literal: Iron was produced; three hundred households were assigned to mine and smelt, delivering tribute with the tax levy.
idiomatic: Iron was mined; three hundred households smelted ore and delivered tribute with taxes.

literal: Xian Prefecture, Andong Army, lower, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Xian Prefecture (Andong Army, lower), military commissioner.

literal: Originally Goryeo Tongshan County land; Bohai established Tongshan Commandery.
idiomatic: Originally Goryeo Tongshan County; Bohai founded Tongshan Commandery.

literal: The land lay north of Han Houcheng County and south of Bohai Longquan Prefecture.
idiomatic: It lay north of Han Houcheng County and south of Bohai Longquan Prefecture.

literal: The land was mountainous and dangerous; bandits made it a lair, so several hundred client households from Ping and Ying prefectures were recruited to build a city and dwell.
idiomatic: Rugged terrain bred bandits; hundreds of Ping and Ying client households were settled in a new garrison city.

literal: At first titled Haoli Grand Guardian Fort; 24 Kaitai year 8 established the prefecture.
idiomatic: First called Haoli Grand Guardian Fort; twenty-fourth note: Kaitai year 8 founded the prefecture.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.
idiomatic: Military affairs to Northern Jurchen Cavalry Command.

literal: Tang Andong Protectorate—in Tianbao era administered between Ying and Ping prefectures; this is that place.
idiomatic: Tang's Andong Protectorate in Tianbao governed between Ying and Ping—this was the site.

literal: Taizu destroyed Bohai and restored the Andong Army.
idiomatic: Taizu destroyed Bohai and restored Andong Army.

literal: In the Kaitai era a county was established.
idiomatic: A county was founded in the Kaitai era.

literal: Xin Prefecture, Zhangsheng Army, lower, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Xin Prefecture (Zhangsheng Army, lower), military commissioner.
Twenty-fifth note: originally Yuexi old fort.

literal: Bohai established Huaiyuan Prefecture; now abolished.
idiomatic: Bohai founded Huaiyuan Prefecture, now abolished.

literal: Shengzong, because the land bordered Goryeo, in the opening of Kaitai established the prefecture and filled it with captured Han people.
idiomatic: Bordering Goryeo, Shengzong founded it at Kaitai's opening with Han captives.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office.
idiomatic: Military affairs to Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office.

literal: Originally Bohai Huaifu County land; carved out from Ping Prefecture Intendant Office and Baoshan County one thousand households to subordinate it.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Huaifu County; one thousand households from Ping Intendant Office and Baoshan County were assigned.

literal: Originally Bohai Baoshan County land; carved out from Ping Prefecture Intendant Office and Rushui County households to establish it.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Baoshan County; Ping Intendant Office and Rushui County households founded it.

literal: Bin Prefecture, Huaihua Army, military commissioner.
In Tonghe year 17 Wuran households were moved; a cishi was placed between the Yazi and Hunton rivers; 26 later it was raised.
idiomatic: Tonghe year 17 relocated Wuran households; a cishi sat between Yazi and Hunton rivers; twenty-sixth note: later promoted.

literal: Military affairs subordinate to the Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office.
idiomatic: Military affairs under Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office.
It had been Bohai Fuyu Prefecture.

literal: Taizu, returning from pacifying Bohai, died here; a yellow dragon appeared, hence the rename.
idiomatic: Taizu died here returning from conquering Bohai when a yellow dragon appeared, prompting the new name.

literal: In Baoning year 7 army commander Yan Po rebelled and the prefecture was abolished.
idiomatic: Baoning year 7: commander Yan Po rebelled and the prefecture was abolished.

literal: In Kaitai year 9 the city was moved northeast; one thousand Han households from Zong and Tan prefectures restored it.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 9 moved the city northeast; one thousand Han households from Zong and Tan prefectures refounded it.

literal: Governing five prefectures and three counties:
Originally Bohai Changping County, with Fuli, Zuomu, and Sushen merged to establish it.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Changping County merged with Fuli, Zuomu, and Sushen.

literal: Originally Bohai Yongning County, with Fengshui and Fulu merged to establish it.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Yongning County merged with Fengshui and Fulu.

literal: Military affairs subordinate to the Eastern Capital army command.
idiomatic: Military affairs under Eastern Capital army command.

literal: Military affairs subordinate to the Eastern Capital army command.
idiomatic: Military affairs under Eastern Capital army command.
